title: Forgiveness
lead: God forgives sins out of mercy, and those he forgives must forgive others. The Bible links the two again and again, from the prayers of Israel to the Lord's Prayer and Jesus' parable of the unforgiving slave.

sections.b: Israel knew God as one who forgives wrongdoing (Exodus 34:6–7; Psalm 103:3, 10–12; Psalm 130:3–4) and who promised a new covenant in which he would remember sins no more (Jeremiah 31:34). The sacrifices of the Day of Atonement dealt with Israel's sin before God. Jesus forgives sins on his own authority (Matthew 9:2–6) and ties God's forgiveness to ours (Matthew 6:12, 14–15; Matthew 18:21–35; Luke 6:37). The apostles preach forgiveness through his death and resurrection (Acts 2:38; Ephesians 1:7) and urge believers to forgive one another as God in Christ forgave them (Ephesians 4:32; Colossians 3:13).
